1.1: Concerning what befell them at the hand of Meqabis among the Jews in Mesopotamia of Syria; and he slew them utterly, to the border of Jerusalem, from Jabbok and from Ṭəfʿa, to the holy precinct.
1.2: For they rose up from Samaria, even to the border of Jerusalem and all its environs, and slew with the edge of the sword, until none remained except the transgressors. For there joined the Edomites, and the Tyrians, and the Amalekites, with Moab — Meqabis, who destroyed the city of Jerusalem.
1.3: And when the children of Israel sinned, He sent against them the Moabite, Meqabis, and he slew them, all of them, with the sword.
1.4: And because of this the anger of the Lord was kindled against His holy city, and they mustered in their camp.
1.5: And the Edomites and the Elofəli rose up, and seized and took vengeance upon the city of God; for by night He sent them, because they had despised the word of the Lord.
1.6: And as for Meqabis — his city was Remat of Moab — and he rose up with strength from his city, and mustered with those who were with him.
1.7: And they saw all the hosts of Mesopotamia to Syria, [come] to destroy the city of God. And from there he sought the Elofəlians and the Amalekites, and gave them much silver and gold, and horses and chariots, that they might be with him in the camp.
1.8: And they came in force, and besieged the city, and shed blood like water — the blood of those who dwelt within her.
1.9: And he made Jerusalem like a miller's trough, and made within her filth and dung and every thing displeasing to God — a deed of affliction — and defiled the city of God, which was full of righteousness and holiness.
1.10: And they made the corpses of Your servants food for the birds of heaven, and the flesh of Your saints to the beasts of the desert.
1.11: And they mocked the meek, O you children of death; and they ripped forth what was in the womb, until God — who tries the heart and the reins — shall have mercy [and intervene]. For those who have no fear of God did according to what Satan taught them.
1.12: And they returned into their tents, rejoicing over the evil they had done to the people of God; and He took away the shelter and the refuge which I had chosen, from the holy city.
1.13: And when they entered and came into their dwellings, they kept Passover and faḥəl and encamped.

2.1: And thus says the prophet, the seer, who says to him: Now rejoice, O sinner, in the hour of light; but now the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, will avenge Himself upon you, because shame never touched your face.
2.2: Our couriers and my horses are worn out, and therefore I have fled to Bedir.
2.3: And I — through you — from ʾänəsərət they run who pursue you, and you shall not escape from them, nor from the stroke of the Lord which is upon you.
2.4: And they said to us: "Gird on the sword; and the drawing of the bow shall not hold me back, nor the därəb of my kwəyan; and I will ʾäkəkoki you; likewise with the därəb of the sword which shall not avenge you," says the Lord, the Holy One of Israel. But there shall come a severe disease into your heart, which is worse than the drawing of the bow, and than the därəb of kwənat, and than the stroke of siḥ — and it shall not ʾäbäq.
2.5: And a severe disease shall come into your heart, and you shall miss him who would help you, and he shall not be found; for I will lay my stroke upon you, and you shall not escape from my hand, until I destroy your remembrance from the earth.
2.6: And He said to me: I am the Lord your Creator. When I do this thing swiftly, like the twinkling of an eye — for you have girded your loins and lifted up your head against My city — for you are like stubble before the wind, which the fire devours before My eyes, and like dust which the winds take up and scatter from the face of the earth; so you are in My hand.
2.7: For I will lay my stroke upon you, and your Creator shall have no mercy upon you; and I will not spare anything that is in you, and none shall remain that hides itself in all your mountains.
2.8: And now repent from all the evil which you have done; and if you have repented and humbled yourself before the Lord with sighing and weeping, and have asked of Him with a pure heart — the Lord will forgive your sin in everything in which you have sinned before Him.
2.9: And at that time Meqabis wept before the Lord because of his sin, and clothed himself with dust; for the Lord had mercy upon him.
2.10: And I understood that God will not delay the evil which He spoke by the mouth of His prophet; for His eyes are watchful and do not sleep, and His ears are open and are not deaf. And I heard the word which He spoke, and He will do it at once, like the twinkling of an eye.
2.11: And he tore off his garment, and put on rough sackcloth, and cast dust upon his head, and wept, and cried aloud before the Lord his God, because of the evil which he had done.

3.1: And the prophet spoke, for Remat of Moab was near to Syria.
3.2: And he tore at the ground, and came even to his loins, and wept with bitter weeping, and repented because of the sin which he had done before the Lord.
3.3: And thus said the Lord to the prophet: Go to the land of Judah; enter; go to the land of Remat, to Meqabis the prince of Moab, and say to him: Thus says the Lord: For it was not of your own hand that you did this — that you should devour by the strength of My might and by My təʿyənət  — you have destroyed the holy city; but I am the Lord; My messenger is with you; of Myself, by My will, I sent you, that you should destroy My city.
3.4: For from My ʿəʿat  with all səsəʿət  and fornication and deceit.
3.5: And I took hold and preserved you alive, and set you in your place; and not by yourself — in which you girded your loins — and you said: "I will rodək  it, the city, by the strength of my hand." And now, because of your children whom you have begotten, the Lord will forgive your sin.
3.6: And now repent with all your heart, and be steadfast, and do not be negligent; for the negligent do not attain to repentance.
3.7: And blessed are those who repent with all their heart, and do not return to affliction and sin, in all their repentance for their evil.
3.8: And they attain with weeping and sighing, and with much prayer, and with worship to the Lord who zäfä ṭäromu ; for He says to the penitents: You — after you have erred and have repented — ʾəliʿayä , you.
3.9: And to the proud He says: After he has sinned, when he comes to Him in repentance, because of your contrition and because of your fear, He will forgive your sin. For I am the Lord, a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children to the third and to the fourth generation; but to those who love Me and keep My commandments I do mercy with them, to a thousand generations.
3.10: And now, because of these your children whom you have begotten, keep My covenant which is with you; and I have accepted the repentance which I have brought about, because of the evil of your deeds, says the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, who kəluyəmäləkə .
3.11: And at that time he went out from gəb , and worshipped the prophet, saying: "Such and such — may the Lord grant me to inherit, that I not be cut off from you; but grant me what you will. For I have despised God, and have not walked in His commandment, as my fathers [did not]; for we have no law. And moreover you know that we serve idols, as our fathers taught us."
3.12: And I — I have not heard the word of His prophets of God until now; for I have sinned, who have walked in my sin, and in the pride of my heart, and in the girding of my loins, in which I despised the commandment of God; and I have not walked in His commandment, nor kept that which He commanded me.
3.13: And the prophet spoke again and said to him: I have understood that now your repentance is accepted; for there is none among you of your kindred who any longer trusts in his sin.
3.14: And from now on forsake the worship of idols, and return into the counsel of God, that your repentance may be in truth. And he worshipped at the prophet's feet; and the prophet raised him up, and commanded him all that is fitting — good deeds.
3.15: And he did according to what God commanded him, and entered into his house.
3.16: And Meqabis set himself aright, and removed from his house all sägäl , and idols, and marəyan , and məṭəʿawəyan , and mäsägəlan .
3.17: And the children of Ṣewan, whom he had brought from Jerusalem — he examined them śärkä , and declared to them all the commandment of God, and His law, and His ordinance, according to what their fathers had done them.
3.18: And he set over his house wise men, from the children of Ṣewa.
3.19: And moreover, from the young among their wise men he appointed [teachers] [supplied] — those who keep — that they might teach them the way of God, according to what the children of Israel did His law and His ordinance and His statutes, and all their abominations which the Moabites yətəḥeräm  — let him hear from the children of Ṣewa.
3.20: And he shattered their abominations, and all their sägälat , and all their idols, and all their mäwaṣəḥt , and their məśəwaʿ , from their səbuḥ , from the ḥäragit  of his märaʿəy , and from the mäqwəʿal  of ṭäli , which he sacrifices to his gods — śärkä ; and he declared.
3.21: And he sacrifices to them, and worships them in every deed, continually; and he asks of them, and believes in them, and does their will in all that the ministers of his gods tell him.
3.22: And he did not turn aside from their words in all that they told him; for it pleased him in all that they had done for him.
3.23: But as for Meqabis, who was among them — he forsook the way.
3.24: And when the seer heard the word which the prophet had spoken to him, he set his way straight into repentance; and all his household made their way straight, [learning] from the children of Israel, at that time. For the children of Israel — at one time they show mercy to him, and at another they chastise him; they teach him, and turn him to the Lord.
3.25: And when He saw that they were humbled under the hands of those that oppressed them, and they cried out before Him — then the Prince teaches them, remembering the covenant of their fathers, when they cry to Him, for the sake of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, their fathers.
3.26: And after He had saved them, they forgot Him who had saved them, and returned to the worship of idols.
3.27: And the Prince sends against them peoples that oppress them; and when they oppress them and afflict them, they cry out to the Lord. And at that time He teaches them, and forgives them; for He loves them, for they are the work of His hands.
3.28: And again, when He gives them rest, they return to seek favor from it, with the worship of the idols which ʿawədomu ; and the work of their hands was evil.
3.29: And He raises up against them the peoples of Elofəli, and Moab, and Midian, and Syria, and Egypt; and they weep and cry out when their məʿw  oppresses them, and he afflicts them, and subdues them, and takes possession of them. And He raises up for them judges, that the judges might save them.

4.1: And there was [one] who believed: Hosea.
4.2: And there was [one] who believed: Gideon.
4.3: And there was [one] who believed: Samson, and Barak, and Deborah, and Judith — whether among women, whether among the humble — He raises up for them judges, that they might save them from those that oppress them, and that He might save them from the hand of all their oppressors.
4.4: And according to what He willed, the Lord saved them from those that oppressed them.
4.5: And they rejoiced greatly in all that He set straight for them: in the sowing of their land, and He multiplied their cattle, and in all pasture that is in the field and in the desert.
4.6: And He blesses for them their cattle, and their plantings, and all that they hold, whether of the house or of the desert; He blesses for them, and their cattle do not miscarry, for with His eyes He watches over them, and He loves them exceedingly, for they are a generation of the righteous.
4.7: And when they became evil in their deeds, He cast them into the hand of their oppressors.
4.8: And when the Prince slays them, they bethink themselves, and return, and cry out to the Lord God their Creator.
4.9: And when they return with all their heart, He forgives them, and their former iniquity He does not do remember to them; for He remembers that they are flesh and blood, and in them is the anointing of the conscience of this world, and devils.
4.10: And Meqabis, when he heard this word which God ordained on the mount of His sanctuary, contended in repentance.
4.11: And he did not turn aside from doing what he had seen; and he heard this word. And because of all the ḫirut which the children of Israel yəgä bəru — for God forgave them; and when God chastises them, if they keep the commandment, they weep and cry out, and again He forgives them, and they do His commandment.
4.12: And likewise Meqabis made his way straight, and kept His commandment, and walked in the commandment of the Lord God of Israel.
4.13: The Prince, when he heard, and in all that the children of Israel counsel — likewise let him counsel with the keeper of His commandment, to the Lord.
4.14: And he established his house and his children, that they might walk in all his way and in His commandments, to the Lord.
4.15: And the ḥərmät of the Jews which they keep — he too shall keep; and the commandments which the Jews keep, when he hears, likewise he shall do; and the mäbaləʿt which the Jews keep he shall keep, though he is of another people — a Moabite.
4.16: And the tithe he shall tithe; and the firstborn of his cattle, and of his flock, and of his ʿədug, and all that is clean he shall give; and the sacrifices which the Jews sacrifice, likewise he shall sacrifice, facing the way toward Jerusalem.
4.17: And [the offering] for firstfruits, and [the offering] for sin, and the freewill [offering], and the sacrifice of salvation, and the sacrifice of zäləf.
4.18: And the first of the fruits, and the moṣaḥt which the Jews bring forth — likewise he shall bring forth, and give to the Levite whom he has appointed; and all that the Jews do, likewise he shall do. And the lifting of incense.
4.19: And he made märanat and milonat and ṭäräṗezat and däbatərat and baḥrəyat and ḥoṣadat, and kə bəʿa wəguʿä for the holy maḥətot and mänəṭolaʿt, as they do within the holy of holies of Israel, when they keep the feast to the Lord.
4.20: For they walked in His law and in His ordinance; and if God had not kept them alive, He would not have given them into the hand of their oppressors. Thus did Meqabis in all his way.
4.21: And he prays at all times to the Lord God of Israel, that they may be led, and that he may not separate from the congregation of Israel who have chosen and done [His] will.
4.22: And again he prays that He may give seed in Zion, and ʾäbəyat in Jerusalem; and that He may save them from those which He spoke by the mouth of the prophet; and that his repentance may be accepted in everything in which he has repented.
4.23: And he wept before the Lord with sighing, [praying] that He would not destroy his seed from the earth, and that He would keep him in his coming in and his going out.
4.24: And of the peoples of Moab who were under his hand, to Meqabis they listened, that they might believe; for in the right way walk their angels, and they keep judgment, and do [His] will; and they establish judgment in their lands, and their districts are at peace, and they see that he is upright and exceedingly wise, Meqabis.
4.25: And they come to him, and hear the judgment of his righteousness, and his ḫirut  — to Meqabis.
4.26: And in it are many ṭərit, and ʾägəbərət, and ʾäʿəmat, and ʾäʿədug, and camels; and in it are horses that wear the sword.
4.27: And after this he worships the Lord; when he walks in ṣäbəʿ, there is none that moʿo except by night that moʿa.
4.28: But they come with the strength of their gods, that they may ṣäbəʿ him and curse him in the name of their gods; and there is none that yəmäwəʿ him, for he has founded his trust upon the Lord his God.
4.29: And it came to pass, while he did thus, and while he yəmäwəʿ the oppressor, that he brought the peoples under his hand.
4.30: And he avenges the oppressed, and justifies the judgment of the children of death.
4.31: And he receives the meek and the children of death in their affliction; and he satisfies the hungry with his food, and clothes the naked with his garment.
4.32: And he rejoices in his conduct and in the work of his hands; and he gives of that which he has, unstintingly; and the tithe he gives to the house of God. And while Meqabis did this, he rested well.

5.1: And he forsook his ʿəgwäl ; and the young children grew, according to what their father had ordained for them, and kept the ordinance of their house; and all that was among them they observed, and they did not cry nädäy  — O you children of death, and you meek.
5.2: And they feared the Lord, and gave their goods to the poor, and were entreated in everything in which their father had entreated them; and they comfort the meek and the children of death in their affliction, and are to them father and mother, and bear them from the hand of their oppressors, and comfort them in all that befell them — trouble and sorrow.
5.3: And they continued, while thus they did.
5.4: And after him came Ṣiruṣaydan, king of the Chaldeans, and he destroyed all their cities, and stirred them up against the children of Meqabis, and destroyed all their districts.
5.5: And he maḫräk  all their goods, and kiyahomuni ; he seized them and carried them off into his districts — the mäməlakəya  of idols — who do not walk in His commandment nor in His statutes of God, but in all evil and fornication and defilement and səsəʿət  and ṣərəfät ; and they did not remember their God.
5.6: And they devoured all carrion and blood, and the food of wild beasts, and bətək , and everything displeasing to God — [the Ge'ez has a negation here, ʾiyəbäləʿu "they did not devour", which contradicts the vice-catalogue context and is probably corrupt,?] — and they have no law from any of the righteous commandments which are written in the Orit.
5.7: And they did not know the Lord, that He is their Creator and their Savior, who brought them out from their mother's womb, and nourished them as is fitting.
5.8: And they have no law in judgment, who walk in affliction and təʿgələt  and zəmut  and defilement, while they take their father's wife, and their mother's sister; and they do all evil, and take their sisters and their kinswomen; and they have no law.
5.9: And all their ways are gloom and darkness and defilement and zəmut .
5.10: But as for the children of Meqabis — they keep, in all that is among them, the təḫrəmət ; and they do not eat carrion nor bətək , nor any of their defilement and their sin, [abstaining] from the children of the Chaldeans. For evil and many are their deeds which are not written in this book, which the children of the ʾÄräbamayan  do — sinners, and the rebellious, hypocrites, and the deceitful, and deceitful ṣiʿ, and defilement, and təʿəgələt.
5.11: And there is nothing upon those who pleases God their Creator.
5.12: And again they worship idols whose name is Beelphegor; and they worship him and believe in him as God their Creator. For he is deaf and dumb, and does not do see nor hears; for a graven image is he, the work of men's hands, which they have säbäk  — nähäbe  silver and gold — the work of the children of ʾəmäḥəyaw , that has no knowledge nor breath.
5.13: And he does not do eat, and he does not do drink.
5.14: And he does not do kill, and he does not do make alive.
5.15: And he does not do plant, and he does not do pluck up.
5.16: He yäḥäsəm not, and he yaśeni not.
5.17: He yanäṣ not, and he yabəʿl not.
5.18: He does not do rebuk, and he does not do forgive; but baḥətu  — ʿəqəfət shall be — for the destruction of the ʿabədan  of the Chaldean people.

6.1: And the proud Ṣiruṣaydan appointed — to the anger of the Lord — lying priests and ministers of idols.
6.2: And they sacrifice to them, and bring [offerings] forth to them.
6.3: And it seems to him that they eat and drink.
6.4: And he gives them, to those who ṣäbəḥ , flocks and cattle and ḥäragit  and ʾäṭäli ; and they sacrifice śärkä , and he declares; and he eats of that defiled sacrifice.
6.5: And not of their own will did they do this to him; but läʾäbəʾəni  they were given and made, that they might eat [of the sacrifices] to their gods.
6.6: And when he saw the children of Meqabis, that they are righteous and worship the Lord their Creator, he desired them; [and] the ministers of the idols yasəḥət them, that they might eat of the sacrifices and eat from that defiled sacrifice. But these blessed ones refused them.
6.7: And he asked them why they refused; for they keep their father's commandment, and are steadfast in good deeds, and fear the Lord exceedingly.
6.8: And when he was wroth against them, and was stern against them, and afflicted them.
6.9: And they told Ṣiruṣaydan the king that he refuses to worship and to sacrifice to his gods.
6.10: And because of this the king was moved with pity, and grieved, and commanded that they bring them; and they brought them, and he set them before him, and said to them: "Eat you, and worship you my gods."
6.11: And they spoke again and said to him: "As for us, we will not obey you in this matter, and we will not sacrifice to your defiled gods."
6.12: And he threatened them with many tortures, and did not prevail against them; for their hearts were steadfast to the Lord.
6.13: And he kindled the fire, and cast them in; and they delivered up their souls to the Lord.
6.14: And He showed him their life after their death — while they held their swords, məlu ḥätä  — while he slept upon his royal bed by night; and great fear [came upon him].
6.15: And he said to them: "What shall I do for you? My ʾägaʿəzt  — bəqwəʿuni  — and I will not lift it for myself, that I may do all that you commanded me; and I will fear Him exceedingly."
6.16: And they told him all that is fitting, saying: "Remember that the Lord your Creator is He; and there is One who shall shatter you from this your pride, and bring you down into Gehenna below, with Diabolos your father. And there you shall fulfill all your judgment, according to what you burned us with fire — while there was none that had sinned against you — and while we worship the Lord our Creator, and worship Him in fear of the Lord."
6.17: For He is the Creator of all, who made heaven and earth and sea, and all that is in them.
6.18: The sun and the moon and the stars, and all creatures which God created lälihu .
6.19: And there is no other god besides Him, in heaven above nor in earth beneath, who is able for all; and there is none like to Him, who kills and makes alive, who rebuks and forgives.
6.20: And there is none that escapes from His hand; for He is the mälak  of heaven and earth.
6.21: And there is none that transgresses His commandment [who escapes?] from Him who created him, save you and your məʿlay  and those like you — mäməʿləyan  who have blinded their hearts — they, and Satan your father; and you and your gods shall go down together into Gehenna, from where there is no escape, forever.
6.22: For it was not you by yourself who did this, but Satan your teacher, who taught you this evil deed, that you might be put to shame before us.
6.23: And you have not known the Lord your Creator, and you have lifted up your head as [though you were] the Lord your Creator.
6.24: And you have boasted in the work of your hands and in your idols, until God humble you, and bring you down to the mäfəḥt  of Gehenna; and He will avenge Himself upon you for all the iniquity and sin which you have done upon the earth.

7.1: "Woe to you, you, and those like you, who have not known Him — the Lord who created you — and have not known His commandment and His word; for you shall be cut off, from which no repentance avails, when you are punished in the straits of Sheol."
7.2: "And you shall have no escape from it forever — you and your gods, and those who sacrifice and worship to them as [if they were] God your Creator — to those which have neither soul nor breath, and which do not avenge them that ʾäḥsämä  them, and show no mercy to them that ʾäśänäyä  them."
7.3: "For the work of man's hand are they, in whom Satan speaks, to destroy the heart of fools like you, O fool! — that he may bring down you and the ministers of your gods, and those demons that command you, into Gehenna of fire."
7.4: "For you have not known that none profits you; you err and are destroyed."
7.5: "And better than you shall be the beasts which God created for your food — and the oxen witəni  and the dogs käläbatəni  — for they have no judgment again, except one death."
7.6: "But as for you, you shall die, and be judged again in the terror of Gehenna, from where there is no escape forever."
7.7: And when they had said this, they departed and were hidden from him.
7.8: And Ṣiruṣaydan was in great fear and trembling, and it did not leave him until morning.
7.9: And then he went to where he had cast the bodies of the righteous, and did not find them; for he desired to yəqä  with them and səʿän  them. For God had hidden them, that he should not təḫaśəś  from their flesh.

8.1: And he went in pride and in təməyənət  of heart.
8.2: For the sun stood in the midst of heaven until he destroyed the armies of the Canaanites and the Hivites and the Hittites and the Perizzites and the Jebusites; and he slew them, and bound their feet in their fetters, and slew them with the edge of the sword, and wəsät  in the bäʿat , and heaped stones upon them.
8.3: And he went about in all ʿəbäd  and evil and hukät .
8.4: And what we told before them: he plows and he nagwʿ  and he eats.
8.5: The kings in one bäʿat  — and by his prayer he made the sun stand at Gibeon, that he might destroy their armies; and he slew in one moment.
8.6: And he did not know God, that He is his Creator — who says: "My time has become as the time of heaven."
8.7: And he thought in his heart that from him the sun rises.
8.8: And he rose up bägod  and encamped in the land of Zebulon, and took ṣ́äbʿa  and Macedonia, and took provisions from Samaria, and gave it to ʾäsäbäʾəməsorəya .
8.9: And he yäḫdr  to the däwäl  of Kedar, and extended to Sidon, and did  gəbər in Achaia, and raised  kəśad  to the Sea of Tekeze, and yətmäyṭ , and sent his messengers to the Indian Sea.
8.10: And thus he raises kəśad  to heaven.
8.11: And his head is not ʾätəḥt  but [he is] in all evil and təzəḫrət .
8.12: And all his ways are in däḥṣ́  and darkness and pride and ʿələwät  and qəṭəqaṭe  and kəʿiw  of blood.
8.13: And all his fəmot  which God hats, he does — according to what Säbəlanəyos taught him, mämə həru  for evil and təʿgələt  and ṣug ; and he yagʿər  the children of death, and does not do pity nädäy .
8.14: And the kings of the nations he brought under his hand, and slew them.
8.15: And the angels of the enemies he judged; and many nations he ʾägrär , and did with them as he willed.
8.16: And he did not spare, and there was none that escaped, from the Sea of Tarshish to the Sea of ʾIyariko .
8.17: And he worships idols, and eats dead things and blood and bətk , and sacrifices to the gods; and in his heart there is no justice, but in all his ways there is nothing except fətəḥ  and mäʿat  and qwəṭʿa  and häkäk . For he became a mädänəgṣ  to the nations under his hand, and did with them as he willed.
8.18: And there is no fear of God before their eyes; for all that he ʾädämo * yəgä bərə  before him, and he walks in təməyənət  before God his Creator.*
8.19: And he regards Him not, that his God, even the Lord, will requite him according to what he did evil against his neighbor, when the day shall seize him with his mäʿat .
8.20: And He will avenge Himself in His time, according to what He śäräw  the former sinners; for He says: "I am the Lord, who avenge Me upon the proud, who do not walk in My commandment; and I will root out their memorial from the earth."
8.21: And the wicked shall be requited according to what they did evil.
8.22: But as for the doers of good, goodness shall be given to them from the Lord.
8.23: And according to what He ʾiyas  destroyed the kings of Canaan in one day, to
8.24: Thus shall He find those who despise God by their evil deeds.

9.1: And you, O man — and God is not [with you?] — why do you exalt yourself, you who today are a man, and tomorrow shall be earth and ashes, and shall become wood and boards in your grave?
9.2: And the [depths?] of Sheol shall be given to you, and to those who do your works; for your teacher Säbəlyanos has revealed, who brought upon his head the sin of all the world, because he caused our father Adam to err through his pride.
9.3: For he who refused to bow down to the work of his God, in the pride of his head and in the loftiness of his kəśad .
9.4: And you, like your teacher, have refused to bow to the Lord your God.
9.6: And vengeance was taken upon them, and they went down into Sheol, because of the evil of their deeds which they did upon the earth.
9.7: And you, like them, shall go down into Gehenna.
9.8: You imagine to snatch from His hand — from God! — for mäʿato  and häk  and tähäk : the worship of God, which gave you dominion over [all?].
9.9: And He proved you, whether you would do His will or not; and if you have made your way straight upon the earth, God shall prosper your paths, and all that your hand has gotten He shall prosper, and shall bless you; and all your adversaries and your enemies He shall destroy for you.
9.10: And you shall rejoice in your ṣ́aʿat  and in your bäʿat , and in the fruit of your belly, and in your storehouses, and in your pastures; and wherever you put forth your fingers, and all that He has put in your heart shall be commanded to you — for from God it was commanded to you. Thus shall you do, and build, and plant, and tənəśət **
9.11: But if you have refused to hear His word and His law of God, and have not walked in His judgment, you have nowhere to snatch from His hand — from God! — like all the rebellious who were before you, who did not worship God in purity, and did not trust in His righteous judgment; for righteousness is all His judgment.
9.12: And there is none that hides himself from before His eyes; and all is naked and manifest before Him.
9.13: Now His is the dominion of kings, and He is the overturner of the thrones of the mighty.
9.14: And He is the exalter of the humble, and the raiser of the fallen.
9.15: And He is the looser of the prisoners, and the raiser of the dead; and those whose flesh is worn out and become as dust, He shall awaken them at the time He wills — for He is an overshadowing of mercy from Him.
9.16: But those who did evil, He shall raise them — a däyən  resurrection — for they despised [God], and He shall requite them.
9.17: And upon the earth He shall yamasən  their seed; for the rebellious are they, against the law and the ordinance of the Lord God.
9.18: And let not sinners plot in their counsel against the righteous; for strait is their path for the righteous, [far] from the ways of sinners.
9.19: And as heaven is high above the earth, so far are the ways of the righteous from the ways of sinners.
9.20: But as for the ways of sinners: the doing of ṣug  and təʿəgələt  and iniquity and fornication and deceit and səsəʿət ; and going after strange property, and drunkenness in iniquity.
9.21: And räwiṣ  in the käʿəwät  of blood, and ʾamasən  in that which is unclean; and səʾanəbəʿa  the children of death; and eating carrion and blood, and eating the flesh of ḥarawəyan ; and the camel and the ḥawir  in a woman ḥaräsä , and təkət  which is not cleansed.
9.22: And all these are the deeds of sinners: broad is the way, and wide is the net of Satan, which leads into ḫaʾgʷäl  and into eternal judgment.
9.23: But as for the ways of the righteous: narrow and mäqəʿan , which lead to life — humility, and yähawət , love and peace, fasting and prayer, and purity of flesh, and abstinence from unclean foods: carrion and bətk  and fornication, and ḥawir
9.24: And they abstain from every foul deed, and from foul foods which are not [permitted?] in the law, and from foul deeds which God does not do love — for all these do the sinners.
9.25: But the righteous are set apart from all evil ways, which God does not do love.
9.26: And He loves them, and has mercy upon them, and shall deliver them from all their tribulations.
9.27: But as for sinners, Satan shall qänəy  them; for they have transgressed His law and His ordinance, and [all] that He loves.

10.1: And you, O kings and rulers, do not walk in his ways, but fear you the Lord God, who created you and has kept you until now.
10.3: For Balak, son of Zippor, when the children of Israel came by the way of Amalek, to inherit the land of the Canaanites and the Hittites and the Perizzites.
10.4: And he said to Balaam: "Curse them for me; for whom you curse is cursed, and whom you bless is blessed. And I will give you much gold and silver, which shall honor you, that you curse them for me."
10.5: And Balaam came, while he looked for his iniquity; and Balak son of Zippor showed him where the children of Israel were encamped
10.6: And he performed divination, and offered sacrifices, and slew bulls and rams, from their səbuḥ ; and he desired to curse the children of Israel.
10.7: But God did not will that he should curse them; but He turned the curse into blessing, by His own word.
10.8: And He said: "Those who bless you shall be blessed, and those who curse you shall be cursed; for you are the people of God, whom He has chosen; and you are the dwelling of the Beloved who comes from on high."
10.9: Then Balak son of Zippor was grieved and angry and enraged, when he [Balaam] blessed them before him, though he had commanded him to curse them.
10.10: And Balaam said to him: "I will not curse those whom God has blessed; for the people whom God has chosen is come into this land."
10.11: And Balak son of Zippor said to Balaam: "I desired that you should curse them for me, but you have not cursed them; but blessing, you have blessed them exceedingly before me. And I — the fullness of my house, gold and silver, would I have given you, if you had said 'Give me,' and had cursed them for me. But you, blessing, have blessed them, and have done me no good; and I will do you no good."
10.12: And Balaam said: "I cannot transgress nor alter the word of God; but what God has set as a word in my mouth, that will I speak."
10.13: And I will not stake my goods upon my life; for had I coveted my goods, God had mercy upon me, that I should not curse the blessed people.
10.14: For God said to Jacob their father: "Those who bless you, blessed let them be; and those who curse you, cursed let them be. For every one that blesses you is blessed."
10.15: But he who curses you without cause is cursed. Make straight your deeds and your ways, that God may love you.
10.16: and do not be like the former people, who despised God by their evil; and He täḥäyäyomu  them — and there are those whom He destroyed by the waters of ʾAyəh [the Flood?].
10.17: And there are those whom He destroyed by the hand of their enemies; and He brought an enemy, an evil people, who took them captive, and led away their kings with their prophets and their Levites.
10.18: And He brought them to a strange land which they did not know, and scattered them, and maḫarək-ed them, and qäśäf-ed them, and ʾamasän-ed their land.
10.19: And they made Jerusalem a ruin, as a field; for they took the ṭəqom  and qəṣər  from the holy city.
10.20: And the priests were led away, and the law was rent, and they fell into the hands of kwənat .
10.21: And the ʿəberat  were led away, and none wept for their dead that died; for they were carried off, and [it was] upon their heads
10.22: And the children wept, and the ʾäʿərug  were täḫaḏfəru ; and they [the invaders] did not pity the face of the elder nor the aged.
10.23: And not those in the assembly, and not dənagəl  — and they ʾamasänu-ed all that they found within their cities, and ʾafəläs-ed them to a strange land which they did not know. For when God willed, wrath came upon His people; He yaqädəm-ed the näśət  of His sanctuary.
10.24: And therefore, when God täḥäyäyomu  the children of Israel, God made Jerusalem a ruin; it shall be plowed as a field — for at all times they despise their Creator.
10.25: But He will not destroy them utterly; for He will spare them for the sake of their fathers — and not for their own sake does He spare them — but because He loves their fathers: Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, who reigned in righteousness, and ḥoru * dəmeyəhu  in righteousness toward their Creator.*
10.26: And He has set them in the məkəʿəbit  of glory, both in heaven and on earth.
10.27: And likewise you, O kings and rulers, who are in this passing world — remember you those before you, who ḥoru  in purity, that they might inherit the kingdom of heaven; and their name is comely from generation to generation.
10.28: And you, that your kingdom may be established and your name prosper, like those before you, the good kings, who pleased God by the goodness of their lives.

11.1: From among them — and not their ʾaṣəmət  and not their ʾaləba  — that which is not a brazen censer, which they brought into the house of God by the command of God; for He said: "Their censers are hallowed, by the offering of their bodies."
11.2: And for me, O sinner, grant me forgiveness; for I have done evil before You. And for these, śəräy  to them; for You are merciful and forgiving.
11.3: And thus He ʾastäśərəyä  to them, to those who ḥämäyəwo .
11.4: And for this, Phinehas was zealous.

11.6: But those who transgressed, the sons of Korah — the earth swallowed them, and brought them down alive into Sheol, in soul and in flesh, with their households and their cattle; and all, every one, according to what he spoke, it was done to him — for he loved the Lord his God, and did not transgress His commandment.
11.7: And likewise you — if you do not transgress the commandment of God, God will do your desire for you, and will love your word, and will keep your kingdom.

11.9: And they said to him: "Are we not sons of Levi, that we should do the work of the priesthood in the chosen tabernacle?"
11.10: And they took their censers to burn incense; and they went and offered incense, but God did not accept their prayer. And by the fire of their censers they were burned and consumed, like wax that melts in the fire; and none was left
11.11: And therefore God said to Moses and to Aaron: "Gather you their censers into the tabernacle; and let it be for My house, its gəbərih ; and all that I have appointed for it, from its entrance to its interior."
11.12: And the ʿaśänäy  of its gəbərih  for the holy tabernacle: məsəḥal , ḫoṣadät , kirub , ʾabəḥərt .
11.13: And mäqdəḥ , and mäsawər , and mäwadəd ; and he bound the gädəgädən  for the ṣaḥərat  tabernacle; and mäś waʿət , which they offer in the chosen tabernacle.

11.16: And let them not provoke jealousy in their God, that His name may be glorified over them, in the tabernacle of His law, of the Lord their God, who ʾasäfəwomu , that He might give them the inheritance of their fathers — a land in which flows milk and honey, which He sware to Abraham.
11.17: And He täkayädä  to Isaac, and established a covenant to Jacob.
11.18: And to Moses and to Aaron, in the tabernacle, säməʿ .
11.19: And to Samuel and to Elias, in Jerusalem, in the tabernacle, in the house of the sanctuary which Solomon built — that it should be the house of God, and the resting-place of His name for the Most High, and the dwelling of the Holy One of Israel.
11.20: For an example and a məstəsəraəy  is this sin, where He shows to His priests, to those who walk in yəwaḥat .
11.21: And where He hears the prayer of those who do His will.
11.22: Where He appoints His law — of the Lord, the Holy One of Israel.
11.23: And where there is made ṣənəḥəḥ  sacrifice, and incense for a pleasing aroma, to the Lord, the Holy One of Israel.
11.24: And it is proclaimed upon the height of məsəḥal , in the chosen tabernacle; and He shows His praise to God, to His chosen, the sons of Jacob, and His holy ones who walk in His commandment; and His judgment is God's.
11.25: But those who yətəʿeyäru  shall be as the sons of Korah, whom the earth swallowed; and likewise the sinners who are like them shall be cast into the judgment of the burning fire, from which there is no escape forever.

12.1: Woe to you, mighty men of Israel, who have not kept what I commanded you in the tabernacle, and have not done [His] will — but your own will: pride and təzəḫərt  and fornication and səsəʿət  and drunkenness and drink and mäḥali  in ḥasät .
12.2: And therefore shall My wrath burn upon you, like stubble before the face of fire, and like fire which burns the mountains, and like a whirlwind which lifts the ṣäbäl dəkum  from the earth and scatters it to the height of the air, where no ʿaśər  of it shall be found from its deeds.
12.3: And likewise will I destroy them, all of those who do evil from before My face, says the Lord, the Holy One of Israel. And remember you God, who rules over all, and there is none who resists Him.
12.4: And He loves those who love Him, and forgives them their sins and their evils, for those who walk in His commandment. and do not be dənəṣəwan  and dənəzuzan  of heart, in unbelief.
12.5: And make straight your souls to God, and be like to Him, that you may save your souls; and I will save you from the hand of your enemies in the day of your tribulation.
12.6: And when you are täṣewəʿu-ed, I will say to you: "Behold, I am with you; and I will save you from the hand of your enemies, and you shall not be təḥeyäy-ed in the day of your tribulation" — for you have trusted in Me, and have done My commandment, and have not transgressed My law, and have loved what I love, says the Lord who rules over all.
12.7: And those who love Him, He loves them; and those who keep His commandment, He has mercy upon them — for He is merciful and forgiving.
12.8: And great is the mäyəṭ  of His wrath, yet He does not do burn with all His mäqəśäfət ; for He is merciful. For He knows that they are flesh and blood; and when their souls go forth from their flesh, they enter into their earth.
12.9: And they do not know where they were, until when God willed to bring them from where they were not; for He created them from where they were not. And again He took their souls, and brought the earth into its märsət .
12.10: And again He will bring them from where they were not into the being of His will.
12.11: And Ṣiruṣayədan, his ʿaḏlawi  to God, greatly täʿabəyo  before God; and when he ḫaḏdägo  until the time of His will, he lifted up his head.
12.12: And he said: "Let my days be as the days of heaven; and I am he who makes the sun to rise, which shall not die forever."
12.13: And while this word was not yet finished, the angel of death came down, whose name is Ṭələmyakos; and he struck his heart, and he died in that hour. And he was täʾagʷälä  from the beauty of his dwelling, and from the greatness of his pride, and from the evil of his deeds — because he did not know his Creator.
12.14: And the army of the king of the Chaldeans, while they were at the entrance of his city, and təʿəyənt  while they desired his ṣäbiʿot  — and when he died, they went forth and destroyed his city, and mahərəku-ed all his ʾənsas , and did not leave until he found no rest in ʿarəfət .
12.15: And all his goods they mahərəku-ed, and qwäsaqwəs  they took; and they burned his city with fire, and entered into their own land.

13.2: And they gave their souls to the fire [martyrdom], that they might be saved from the fire of heaven; they knew that this world passes away.
13.3: And he said to me: "And no delight dwells for zəluf ; for they knew that more grievous is the təʿəyərt  of God than the təʿəyərt of the servants of the living, and more grievous is the wrath of God than the wrath of the king."
13.4: And He reckons one day — they shall rejoice in the ʾaʿəṣədat  of Paradise — than a thousand years of life upon earth; and for long days He reckons one hour. Forgive  ziʾakä , O my Lord.
13.5: Their hands [are] good who ḫəburä ; they gave their souls to death. They knew that təśeniyuḫarit  is their life, rather than this earthly, passing one.
13.6: But You, O my Lord, remain forever; and Your years which shall not fail, and Your memorial from generation to generation.
13.7: And all this, and the like, ḥaläyu  the sons of the Meqabyan; and they ʾabdäru-ed and ʾabdäru-ed, trusting in God, and refused the polluted sacrifice of liḥa .
13.8: And therefore they gave their flesh as wax for God's sake. They knew that the dead shall rise, and they knew that there shall be judgment after the resurrection.
13.9: But those who do not know and do not believe the resurrection of the dead — they knew
13.10: And He showed them that all passes away; and they gave their souls to death, that from God they might find məzəgana  — because they believed in Him, and did not bow to idols, and did not eat the sacrifice of the dead and of pollution.
13.11: And therefore they knew that He will make them rejoice in the latter day, in soul and in flesh. For while they were with wife and children, they did not know the taste of this world, nor the bitterness of death; and they gave their souls to death. They knew that there shall be a resurrection in the latter day, in soul and in flesh.
13.12: And they knew that they shall reign — who kept the ordinances of God — in the world to come, for generation to generation, and for long days, where there is no sickness and no sorrow.
13.13: There, there is no sickness and no sorrow, and no death; and with those who believed in the word of God — the chosen kings and rulers — and gave their souls to death, like wax in the midst of fire, while they beheld with the mind of their heart that which is to come.
13.14: And they shall shine, zäyəbərəh  their faces, sevenfold more than the sun; and that they may rejoice in His love at the resurrection of all, in soul and in flesh.

14.1: As for me, it grievs me exceedingly, and it yatekəz  me and yəqäləy  my heart, concerning the Judahites and Samaritans and Pharisees and Sadducees, who do not believe the resurrection of the dead. The Judahites say: "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die; and thereafter we shall see none."
14.2: And the Samaritans say: "Our flesh shall not rise, for it shall become dust."
14.3: But if there be a resurrection — we believe in the resurrection of our souls; for the soul, when the flesh dies, does not do dy. For it is as the wind, which is not seen, and as the sound of thunder; and none can speak it nor show it.
14.4: But our flesh is seen by all, and becomes ashes and dust; for the beasts devour it, and the ʿəṣeyat  devour it in the grave.
14.5: And as for those who devoured it, they become ashes, and no ʿaśər  of them is found; for they become as grass, and as though they had never been created, they become ashes.
14.6: And by this are found the bodies which bäləyu  And thus say the Pharisees: "We believe in the resurrection of the dead; but He will clothe the souls in the heavens with another flesh than that which was on earth."
14.7: And thus say the Sadducees: "When our soul goes forth from our flesh, we shall not rise from the dead; and they have no resurrection of the dead — neither for soul nor for flesh. And when we die, we shall not rise."
14.8: And for this they err exceedingly, and it yatikəz  me concerning them; for they speak ṣərəfät  against God and His praise.
14.9: And they have no hope of salvation, for they did not believe in God who would justify them; but they have no hope of salvation and of the resurrection of the dead.
14.10: And O blind Judahite, you have tasätäʿabəyinu  against God, who brought you from where you were not who sowed you, He ʿabəqulo  your soul and your flesh, in His likeness and in His image.
14.11: And think you not thus; for you shall not escape from His hand. To God you shall rise, how while you do not desire; and you shall be judged while you do not love. For the cord of Sheol is in your kəśad , which seizes you until the day of your death.
14.12: For in the belly you shall təśärəf  for yourself; from the gunəd  of Sheol is this cord, which you let down into your kəśad ; and when you tələḥəq , so too it tələḥəq .
14.13: And when you die, you let it down into your kəśad ; and when the gunəd  draws it, you bring them
14.14: And you draw its ʾaʿəṣuq ; for all the sinners are seized within it, as the cord is in their kəśawəd .
14.15: And He will bring all the souls of the sinners from where they were, from the ends of heaven; and likewise your cord shall draw you, that you may bring your soul from where you were, and you shall enter into the fäläg  of Sheol.
14.16: And your flesh, täʾatito  and wino  sevenfold — as the flesh of our father Adam — the dew of His mercy shall raise you, of God; and thereafter you shall be judged according to what you have done evil and sin, according to what you have not believed.
14.17: And it shall not profit you and you err in your night, who dwell in the grave in your error, and say: "There is no resurrection of the dead" — that they may err from the commandment of God.
14.18: And who shall yäḫaḏəg  you in ashes and earth, that he may raise you, that he may judge you according to your deeds which you have done?
14.19: And then He shall come — from where your spirit which is in the winds, and from where your dust which is in the earth, and from where your flame which is in the fire.
14.20: And from where the spirit of life which was breathed upon you, in the ʿaṣäd  of darkness.
14.21: Which täʿaʿəwaq  but the souls of the righteous in Paradise with joy are yətəʿaṣəwa .
14.22: But you, O Judahite and Samaritan and Pharisee and Sadducee — until the time of your judgment, you shall tətə ʿaśər  in darkness.
14.23: And then you shall see how God shall judge you according to your deeds, because you have ʾasə ḥatäkä luboʾo .
14.24: And you shall say to them: "The dead shall not live; let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die." And you say in your kal , while you sit upon the seat of Moses: "There is no resurrection of the dead."
14.25: And therefore you have erred, while you know the book of the Law, and teach the word of the books; and you cause men to err from ḫaḏsäyäkä , whereas you have not learned and do not know.
14.26: The word of the books — you exalt the people of God with the evil of your teaching, and with your word which does not do profit.
14.27: But you shall be requited according to your deeds, and according to the fruit of your kännafr ; for God is no respecter of persons. And to those who learn good, He will reward them with good things, which He has prepared for those who love Him.
14.28: But you, you have nowhere to escape from His hand, who shall judge you; and behold, He shall judge you according to your deeds. For you and those whom you have mäharək-ed shall be judged.
14.29: I have told you that the dead shall rise. Then those who kept His commandment shall rise; and none shall yətəhakäl  to stand. For His commandment shall bring them forth — as the earth brings forth grass when the rain yəzäbəṭ .
14.30: And as the moist tree brings forth its shoot when the rain waters the earth, and as it brings forth fruit — its root or the ear of grain — and it cannot withhold its fruit in the year God has śämər-ed
14.31: And as conception, when ḥəmam  comes, the womb cannot restrain it but when it hears the voice of God, it bears them for the dew which is from God shall come down upon it.
14.32: And likewise the earth shall bring forth it cannot restrain but when it hears the voice of God, it bears them for the dew which is from God shall come down upon it.
14.33: And the bodies shall be gathered into their places, where their ʾabədənət  fell; and one house of the treasuries of souls shall remain. And the souls shall enter into the bodies, from where they went forth before.
14.34: And at the blowing of the horn, the dead shall rise in the twinkling of an eye; and they shall stand before God, and He shall requite them according to the work of their hands.
14.35: Then you shall see that you shall rise from the dead; and you shall be tanəkər-ed in all your deeds which you did upon earth. And when you see them written before your eyes — and this ʾamirä  you shall tənäsəḥ  — where it shall not profit you.
14.36: And you shall know that you shall rise from the dead; and you shall be judged according to your deeds which you have done.

15.1: But those who heard in their good deeds — then they shall rejoice. But those who täḥäkäyu , while they say "The dead shall not rise" — then they shall grieve, when they see that they are risen from the dead, with their evil deeds, which do not profit.
15.2: And their deeds which they did shall judge them, while there is none to yəwäqəs  them They knew themselves how they shall be judged.
15.3: And they shall stand at the station of the wicked, in the day of weeping and of judgment, in the day of däyən , and in the day of God.
15.4: In the day of darkness, in the day of ṭaqa , in the day of gimi , in the day of ṣäʿəʿ , in the day of lightning.
15.5: In the day of fear and trembling, in the day of dädək  and märəqi , in the day of ʾasäḥatəya .
15.6: In the day the evil shall be requited according to what he did evil; and in the day the pure shall be requited according to what he did purity; and in the day the ṣəwag  shall be requited according to what he did ṣug .
15.7: And in the day the master shall not be honored above the servant, nor the maid above her mistress.
15.8: And in the day the king shall not be honored above the poor, nor the ruler above the child, nor the father above his son, nor the mother above her daughter.
15.9: And in the day the baʿəl  shall not be honored above the näday , nor the proud above the humble, nor the great above the small; for it is the day of justice, and the day of requital and of judgment — the day when He shall requite all according to what he did.
15.10: And the day when the doers of good shall be rewarded; and in the day the evil, who did evil, shall be requited.
15.11: And the day, when they shall rejoice who were rewarded with good; and the day, when they shall grieve who were rewarded with evil. And they shall see those who ʾaḥäsäyu  the books, while they say: "The dead shall not rise."
15.12: Then shall all the sinners of the earth weep for their sins which they did; for there found them a sorrow which has no comfort, because they did not good upon earth.
15.13: And likewise for the chosen also who did good, their joy shall not fail forever and ever; for while they were upon earth, they listened to good deeds.
15.14: And they did not transgress the commandment of their Creator; for they knew that they should rise from the dead.
15.15: And because they did not transgress His commandment, they shall inherit
15.16: And in the heavens He has given them to inherit the land of life, which He sware to their fathers, in the day of resurrection, in the day yənädəyu * ʾabəʿəlt .*
15.17: And they shall yäʾawəyaw  — the doers of evil, who do not believe the resurrection of the dead, nor the law of God; and the day of resurrection they did not remember.
15.18: Then they shall see you shall find them evil, which has no maḫələqət , and which has no healing in it, and no nuzaʾze ; and in their hearts a sorrow which has no comfort, and no rest.
15.19: And ʿəṣe  which does not do dy, and fire which is not quenched.
15.20: And upon their flesh: fire and täy , and a whirlwind, and ḥasätəya , and hail, and dädək  which yəzonəm  upon them.
15.21: Mäqaṣəḥ of fire for those who do not believe the resurrection of the dead.

16.1: According to his work, and according to the cleanness of his hands.
16.2: And from where comes it that you say: "These ṣəfər  of your hands and your feet, and the ṣägur  of your head"? Did not God make them, that they should yəṣaʿ  — that you may know the resurrection of the dead which shall not be in another flesh — that you may know for yourself that you shall rise from the dead.
16.3: And you shall be judged according to your deeds which you have done — evil and sin — at the resurrection of the dead; because you have caused the people to err, while you say: "There is no resurrection of the dead."
16.4: And now you shall see, when the day of your requital comes to you; for what you have sown shall not ʾäʿabi  that it should profit — from where grain and from where root.
16.5: And again, you who have planted a tree — it shall not ʾäʿabu  From where the vine, and from where the fig tree? Its shoot and its fruit shall not be changed.
16.6: And if you have planted a vine, it shall not be changed to become a fig tree; and if you have planted a fig, it shall not be changed to become a vine; and if you have sown a root, it shall not be changed to become sägäm .
16.7: And if you have sown sägäm , it shall not be changed to become a root. All these — in his seed and in his bäzämädu  and in his fruit and in his tree and in his bäqʷäṣəl  and in his bämərəw  — he shall receive blessing by the dew of mercy which is from God, and shall bring forth fruit.
16.8: Likewise the earth shall bring forth that which God has sown; it shall profit soul and flesh — the doers of good, while they are not changed into doers of evil; and the doers of evil, while he is not changed into a doer of good. Those whom God has sown shall profit in soul and flesh.
16.9: And when the time comes for the blowing of the horn, the dead shall rise by the dew of mercy which is from God — who did good — in the resurrection of life; and their ʿəśet  — Paradise of joy — a dwelling for the pure, which He has prepared for the chosen, where there is no disease and no sickness, where they shall not die again.
16.10: But those who did evil — in the resurrection of judgment — with the devil who ʾaləḥat  them.
16.11: And his evil angels who do not desire to be saved, from all the servants of the living — in the judgment which is forever.
16.12: Underneath, beneath, in the ṣənaf  of darkness, where is weeping and ḥaqəyäsənän , where there is no forgiveness and no mercy, and where there is no escape forever and ever — because they did not good in their life upon earth, while they were in their flesh.
16.13: And therefore they shall be judged at the resurrection of soul and flesh.
16.14: For lelomu  — for those who do not believe the resurrection of soul and flesh — with you thus God shall show great is His täʾaməri .

17.1: And the grain of wheat: if it does not do dy, it does not do profit and bears no fruit; but if it dies, the grain of wheat makes root in the earth, and brings forth a shoot, and becomes an ear, and bears fruit; and täʾaməru .
17.2: For you, that there may be many grains — one grain of wheat.
17.3: And likewise this grain profits from wind and water and earth; and the sun fire. For that which is without the sun cannot bear fruit
17.4: And the wind həyənt nädəs ; and that which is without wind cannot bear fruit And the water which yaśäqəya  and waters the earth.
17.5: And when it is watered, dust and earth, it makes root and yətəliḥal  upward, and bears fruit by the ʾaməṭan  of the blessing of God.
17.6: For the grain of wheat is in the likeness of Adam, upon whom was breathed the spirit of God and the vine. Likewise it yəśäqəy  with water, and makes root, and lifts water the cord of fine root.
17.7: And it ascends toward heaven, in the kätämä  of the shoot for the dew of mercy which is from God yaṭəbəw  them in the kätämä * ʾaḥərug  näwaḫatäwəyəbäsəl  by the flame of the sun; and it brings forth fruit which is from God.*
17.8: And it makes a sweet fragrance which makes glad the heart; and in it, when they eat it, it satisfies as water; and bread — it shall not hunger nor thirst. And when yäʿaṣərəwa , it makes dämä ʾaskal .
17.9: And when they drink it, it makes glad the heart of man, as it says in the Psalm: "Wine makes glad the heart of man." And with śəmur  it intoxicates when yabäqəʿ  his mouth and he yəwəḫaṭ  and yəmələʿ  in his sänəbəʿ ; and his blood yətəkäʿaw  in his heart.
17.10: And it yəresəy  the one who is without heart; for the drunkenness of wine causes to err exceedingly. And it yəresəy  him to ṣädəf  and to gʷäṣagʷäṣ  as the broad earth; and he does not do know ʿəqəfət , nor the śok  that is in his hands and his feet.
17.11: And thus God made with the vine and its fruit, that His name may be yətəʾakʷat  — for those who do His will, and for those who believe the resurrection of the dead.
17.12: And He shall make them rejoice in the dwelling of life — for those who believe the resurrection of the dead.

18.1: From what error do you err, O you who do not believe the resurrection of the dead? And when they lead you where you do not know at this time tənəśəḥu  where it shall not profit you; and when they cast you into judgment, because you did not believe the resurrection of the dead, in flesh and soul ḫəburä .
18.2: And you shall be requited according to your deeds, whether good or whether evil; for you have ʾaḥəsäm-ed the heart of your kaləʾan , while you say: "We believe that the dead shall not rise — who became ashes and earth."
18.3: And therefore their neighbors err; for there is no saḥət  for their death, and they cannot məqəś * fətomu  for they shall stand before the judge of God.*
18.4: And they shall be təḫaḏfəru-ed exceedingly, when He yəgeśəṣ  them in His wrath, and He shall yətəmäʿaʿ  them for all the evil which they did. For while they did not know the ways of God, they speak for ləlihomu  they did not know from where they came.
18.5: And they did not know where they go, into the judgment of the burning fire. For according to the ṭəwəyät  of their heart they teach their neighbors; for bitter are they, and gʷäṣagʷäṣ  in their deeds, and ṣäwagan  and those who teach ṭəway * nägär , while they say: "There is no resurrection of the dead."*
18.6: And this ʾamirä  — they knew that the dead shall rise; and they shall be judged, because they did not believe the resurrection of the dead — for all the creatures, the servants of the living.
18.7: For we are all the fruit of Adam, and through Adam we die; for for us all, through the sin of our father Adam, there found us the judgment of death from God.
18.8: And again, as we shall be judged according to what we have done, we shall rise with him, Adam our father; for through our father Adam's not knowing, täqänəy  entered the world to death.
18.9: And therefore we are judged by the transgression of Adam; and our flesh is consumed in the grave, and our bones are täqäṭəqäṭu .
18.10: And the earth sätäyətät  our ʾanəgʷaʿ  and our masän  and our laḥəy  is consumed in ashes; and our flesh is tädäfənä  in the earth, and our good qal  is tädäfənä  in the earth.
18.11: And there went forth ʿəd  from our ʾayənt  shining and our masän  in the mäkab ; and it became dust.
18.12: Where is the beauty of their laḥəy  for the good wärazut  whom Adam qomomu  and śaʿəśaʿ  the taste of their words? Where is their greatness for the ṣənəʿan ?
18.13: And where is their strength for kings, and their honor for rulers? And they were täräsəyo  with horses, and täśärəgəwo  with gold and silver, and täräśəyo  with the goods of the field which yanəṣäbärəq .
18.14: Where is the taste of mäbaləʿət  in sweet wine?

19.1: O earth, that have gathered kings and rulers, and the great and the honored, and beautiful women, and fair virgins.
19.2: And strong hands, in whom was beauty, and fair  ʾaqʷayaṣ ; and in whom was knowledge and ləbuna ; and in whom was a fair voice, like the voice of ʾarəganon näbabit , and like the zəbəṭät  of the harp and ʿənəzira .
19.3: And in whom was fair song, who make rejoice as the drinking of wine, O son of Adam their eyes [were] shining like the morning stars.
19.4: And their yəman  was strong as he who yəhub  and he yənäśəʾ  and yäḥayəṣ  and their feet [were] fair to behold; and for those who yərəwəṣa  like mäkʷərakʷər * rətuʿat .*
19.5: I know you, O Death, who have taken their souls — of the fair hands; for by the will of the Lord God you are täfänäwəkä .
19.6: But you, O earth — for you have gathered many bodies, whom God brought forth from you, and He shall bring them in to you. From you we went forth, and to you we shall enter. By the will of God we täfäśaḥənä ; by the will of God, upon you.
19.7: And you are mändäf  for our limbs; we ʾansosäw  upon you, and we nom  in your wətit . We have eaten your fruit, and you have eaten our flesh.
19.8: We have drunk from the dew of your näqəʿ , and you have drunk from the näqəʿ  of our blood. We have eaten from the ʾanəgʷaʿ  of your earth, and you have eaten from the ʾanəgʷaʿ  of our bones.
19.9: We have eaten from the taste of ashes; your dew is fair, as God commanded you, for our sisit . And you have taken the laḥəy  of our flesh, and you have räsäyəki-ed dust, as God commanded you, for your sisit .
19.10: O Death, from you who have gathered many of us — our mighty ones, kings and rulers — and you did not fear their gərəma  nor their greatness, as He commanded you who created them; and you ʾimänänəkä  the poor.
19.11: And you ʾeməḥərəkä  those whose laḥəy  is fair; and you did not spare the mighty and the strong; and you did not spare the ʾabəʿəlt  and the nədayyan , the ḫaśuman  and the fair ʾaʿərug, and children of ʿədəw, and women.
19.12: And you did not spare those who think good and do not transgress His commandment; and you did not spare those who think evil — who became as beasts in their deeds — nor those who are perfect in the beauty of their laḥəy , and their words, and the taste of their nägär .
19.13: And you did not spare those whose words are bitter, and full of märəgäm  in their mouths; and you have gathered their souls into your treasuries — whether of light or whether of darkness.
19.14: And the earth has gathered their flesh — whether in the kʷäkʷəḥ  or whether in the earth — until the blowing of the horn, when the dead shall rise.
19.15: And the doers shall be judged even according to their deeds which they did; for at the blowing of the horn and at the commandment of God the dead shall rise, in the twinkling of an eye; and they shall rejoice who did good.

20.1: Believe me, that He will spare none and will hide none — [even] all our deeds which we did upon the earth — when we stand before Him in fear and trembling.
20.2: And when we shall be filled with shame for our way, and when we have no garment for our nakedness.
20.3: And when we have no mərəguz  for our hands, nor ʿaśaʿ  for our feet.
20.4: And I do not know his way, where they shall lead us — whether däḫəṣ́ , or gwäṣ́agwəṣ́ , or darkness, or śok ; and moreover, whether the qälay  of the sea or the qälay  of Sheol.
20.5: And those who shall lead us, we shall not know them, and we shall not hear their speech.
20.6: And we shall not see their faces, for they are darkness; and in darkness they shall lead us.
20.7: As said David the prophet: When my soul was troubled within me — You, O Lord, did show my way. In this way I went; I hid my testimony; and I turned aside from the path of my right [hand]; and I saw, and I sinned against him who warned me; and in him I have no ʾämäśəṭ .
20.8: And this he says: for he warns that the demons yəśaläqəwo  him, and lead him to the one who does not do know the way; and he turns aside to the right and to the left; and there is none to find him who would make known.
20.9: And for me there is none to make known, but only in the midst of the angels of darkness.
20.10: And the spiritual angels of light, who are sent to the ḫeran , that they may convey their souls to the righteous, and lead them to the ʿaṣ́äd  of the light of life.
20.11: And those — the angels of darkness and the demons — are sent to the souls of sinners, that they may receive them and lead them away into the eternal judgment which is prepared for them, that they may be judged according to their deeds which they did.
20.12: Woe to them, the souls of sinners, who are led into ḫagwəl ; and there is no rest, and no ʾädəḫin , and they shall not ʾäməśəṭ , and they shall not escape, forever, from the tribulation which has found them.
20.13: Woe to them, the sinners! For in the way of Cain they went, and by the counsel of his error they täḫagulu-ed to Balaam; and the sins which they commit; for bänäśiʾo * hələyanə  they went down, they yəmäkänəyu , that they might take others' goods by violence, which were not their goods.*
20.14: They indeed shall be judged according to their deeds which they did, in the judgment of burning fire.

21.1: Where are those who gathered up others' goods by violence, which were not their goods, and the work of their hands?
21.2: But — for they take others' goods, which are without śiṭ , and gather them up — while they do not know the day of their death. You shall overtake them, and they shall leave to another their bəʿəl .
21.3: And their children shall not rejoice in the bəʿəl  of their fathers; for they are houses of sinners — whether yamänäzəzəwomu , or by theft, or by təʿəgələy ; those like them are sinners, like their fathers; or by ḥäyəd .
21.4: And there is none to preserve for them the goods of their fathers; for in violence they gathered them for themselves. And like the śaḥəw  of a cloud, and like smoke which the wind lifts, and like the fruit of grass which is shaken, and like wax which melts before the face of fire — so shall perish the glory of the sinners.
21.5: As said David: I saw the wicked great and exalted, like the cedar of Lebanon; and when I returned, I ḫaṭaʾəkəwo-ed; I sought him, and did not find his place.
21.6: And likewise is the destruction of the sinners, in məʿər : that they shall not be established, those who oppress their neighbors — though they are not as those who do not die — because they gathered others' goods by ʿa mäṣ́a .
21.7: O servants, remember that you shall pass away, and your bəʿəl  also shall pass away with you; and though [it be] with much of your silver, and your gold also, there shall be that which is left.
21.8: And if you multiply children, there shall be many graves; and if you multiply houses, there shall be mäzəbär .
21.9: And if you multiply cattle, they shall be a spoil to your enemies; for you have not done the will of the Lord God your God. And all that your hands have produced shall not be found, for it is not blessed.
21.10: Whether of the house or of the field; whether with ʾäʿəʿod  and fruit, or with ḥätəl ; or with the produce of ʿəkəl  and məkəyad  and wine.
21.11: And if you do not rejoice in the fruit of your wombs, but sorrow shall be to you from all your enemies; for God shall not prosper you with all the men of your house; for you have not kept the commandments of the Lord God.
21.12: But to those who keep His law and His commandment and His statute, He shall not withhold them from His blessing; and He shall give them all that they ask; and He shall bless for them the fruit of their land and the fruit of their wombs.
21.13: And He shall cause them to inherit the exaltation above all the nations which ʿawədu  them, that they may be [exalted?], and not that they be brought low; and He shall give them all blessing, in their increase and their fruit.
21.14: And all which their hands have produced, He shall bless for them the fruit of their tillage, and the increase of their cattle; and He shall make them rejoice in the fruit of their wombs.
21.15: And He shall multiply for them their cattle, and save them from all their tribulations, from disease and dəkam , and from the mänəsut  of those who know and of those who do not know.
21.16: And He shall stand for them in the midst of judgment, and save them from tribulation and from evil speech and from all that rises up; for at the first he made the tabernacle. If a Levite, who is blameless and strong, keeps the service of the tabernacle and walks in the will of the Lord God — by the former law he [the Israelite] shall give him the tithe of all that comes in, and every firstborn from man even to cattle.
21.17: And a city of refuge in all their lands, as Moses commanded Joshua the son of Nun, that the slayer might be saved who slew unwittingly — or whether wittingly.
21.18: Until they bring him to judgment, to condemn him or to justify him.
21.19: And by your inquiry they shall say to them: "If there was hatred with him—" And he shall say: "For unwittingly there fell from my hand an axe, or a stone, or a tree, and he died, he upon whom it fell." Know this: save him, for unwittingly he did it; he shall be saved.
21.20: But as for him who did it wittingly, he shall be judged according to his sin, and there is none to pity him. But as for him who did it unwittingly — though he killed — by your inquiry, spare him, that he do not die; for unwittingly he did it.
21.21: And thus Moses commanded the children of Israel, that they should not transgress the commandment of the Lord God, but that they should keep themselves from all evil — he commanded them.
21.22: And he commanded them also, that they should walk in all His judgments; and the righteous shall fädəfad  put far from themselves ʾägəʿ  and bətək  and death, and from all that is unseemly for the children of men — that those who walk in the commandment of the Lord God may do them, and those who cease from all evil, as he commanded them.
21.23: And he commanded them, that they should not transgress the commandment which he ordained for them, according to the pattern which came  mayat  — which is the tabernacle — that their souls might be saved, and they might find their rest with their fathers who did good.
21.24: For those who believed in the word of the Lord God, and walked in the commandment — they shall be called təwə lədä  of the righteous; for from Adam and Seth are they, who did the will of the Lord God — we ʾiyəmenənə .
21.25: For we are the seed of Adam; and in His likeness we were läḥäkwänä ; and in His image He created us, that a fine dawn might shine; and all who keep to the Lord God.
21.26: And as for us, we have done good; we shall inherit the land of the living with those who did good — for there is no destruction and no night — for those who love Him.
21.27: And fädəfad  He shall love them, and hear their prayer — for those who call upon Him in purity — and He shall yətəwe * käfə  their nəsəḥ  — for those who are pure in ṭəbuʿ  — and He shall give them might and ṣ́änəʿ , to those who keep His law and His statute and His commandment.*
21.28: And they shall rejoice with Him in the kingdom which is forever — those who did His will — whether first or last; to Him they shall offer the sacrifice of praise, and to ages of ages. Amen.
